# 3. Scope and Goals

## 3.1 In Scope

- Message formats and wire encoding for cooperative perception, intent, group membership, and attestation.
- A normalized perception profile that allows heterogeneous sensor suites to produce interoperable output.
- A trust and security model covering identity, pseudonymity, continuous attestation, misbehavior detection, and revocation.
- A privacy model covering what data may be transmitted, under what conditions, and for how long it may be retained by any participant.
- A fusion framework that produces calibrated confidence in multi-source object tracks.
- Cooperative behaviors: the C-ACC Group Protocol and the optional Slipstream Mode overlay.
- Safety architecture and ISO 26262 ASIL allocation per message class.
- Vehicle integration interfaces to ADAS, gateway ECUs, and telematics units.
- Conformance classes and a self-test framework.

## 3.2 Non-Goals

O-CPS explicitly does not specify:

- New radio physical layers. O-CPS runs on C-V2X PC5 sidelink (LTE-V2X Rel-14/16 and NR-V2X Rel-16+) and on ITS-G5 (IEEE 802.11p / bd) where available. No new PHY is defined.
- New cryptographic primitives. Signatures use ECDSA over P-256 (MUST) and may additionally use Ed25519 (MAY) as defined in IEEE 1609.2-2022 and ETSI TS 103 097 v2.1.1.
- Cloud-dependent control paths. O-CPS is a sidelink-first protocol. Cloud interfaces are OPTIONAL and MUST NOT be in any safety-critical loop.
- In-vehicle HMI design. How a participant surfaces cooperative state to the driver is out of scope. How it gates driver authorization is in scope (§13.1.3).
- Commercial licensing of sensor hardware, compute platforms, or backend services.

## 3.3 Goals

An O-CPS implementation, conformant to this specification, is expected to achieve the following properties. These are design goals, not requirements; the normative requirements that realize them appear in later sections.

- Interoperability across vendors with no prior coordination, provided both sides are conformant to the same conformance class.
- Bounded latency: a PerceptionSummary observed at one participant is available at peer participants within 100 ms at the 99th percentile under nominal channel conditions.
- Graceful degradation: loss of cooperative messages MUST result in a return to local-sensor-only behavior, not in unsafe actuation.
- Cryptographic deniability of individual vehicles’ long-term identity: no O-CPS message, or correlated set of messages, shall reliably identify a specific vehicle over time without possession of a revocation key held by the issuing CA.
- Retrofittability: the baseline conformance class (Class A, §17.1) MUST be implementable on current C-V2X/ITS-G5 hardware without ECU replacement.
